title: Avoid the Bite trade without Blood Vial
situation: When an event offers five Bites and Strike removal in exchange for a large maximum-HP loss, especially without Blood Vial, evaluate the permanent survivability cost before accepting.
lesson: Generally refuse the Bite trade unless Blood Vial or a similarly strong source of mitigation makes the 24 maximum-HP loss worthwhile. Five Bites can provide sustain, but lowering the health ceiling from 80 to 56 makes every later combat and mistake substantially more dangerous.
evidence_points: Act 2 Floor 19: the run accepted five Bites and Strike removal while losing 24 maximum HP, changing from 69/80 HP to 56/56.
The final relic list did not include Blood Vial, while the final deck contained five Bites.
The final Gremlin Leader fight was entered at 39/56 HP and ended in death.
reasoning: The event's benefits were permanent deck improvement and healing access, but the maximum-HP reduction also permanently reduced the buffer available for combat damage. Without Blood Vial to offset that reduction, the trade was a poor risk-reward choice for this run's already attrition-heavy path.

title: Do not treat roughly 70% HP as an automatic reason to heal
situation: At a rest site with about 39/56 HP, distinguish between genuinely dangerous low health and a normal combat-ready health total before choosing rest over an upgrade.
lesson: At 39/56 HP, smithing can be reasonable; the rest-site choice should depend on the upgrade's survival value and the route, not on the percentage alone. The larger strategic priority is avoiding the earlier maximum-HP loss and preventing combat attrition.
evidence_points: Act 2 Floor 23: the run had 39/56 HP and chose to upgrade Shockwave rather than heal.
39/56 HP is approximately 70% of the current maximum, not an automatically critical health state.
The run's maximum HP had already been reduced to 56 by the Act 2 Bite event.
reasoning: The initial reflection over-attributed the outcome to smithing at 39/56 HP. That health level is often adequate for an upcoming fight, whereas the earlier 24-point maximum-HP loss affected every subsequent combat. Resting should still be selected when a specific fight or route makes the extra HP necessary, but this decision alone was not clearly the central mistake.

title: Manage HP proactively when multiple enemies are attacking
situation: During difficult combats, especially after entering with a reduced maximum HP, preserve health by prioritizing block and threat reduction instead of spending the turn almost entirely on attacks.
lesson: Reduce combat attrition through better defensive sequencing: when several enemies have attack intents and HP is already low, play available block earlier unless immediate damage clearly prevents more harm. Do not leave defense as the final action after exhausting energy on attacks.
evidence_points: Turn 9 of the Gremlin Leader fight began at 24/56 HP with Mad Gremlin, Sneaky Gremlin, and Gremlin Leader all showing ATTACK intent and the player at 0 Block.
Defend was legal from the start of Turn 9, but the run first used Wild Strike and two Bites before playing Defend with only 1 energy remaining.
The run suffered substantial combat attrition across the trajectory, including reaching 24/80 after the Act 1 Sentries and 18/80 near the end of the Hexaghost fight.
reasoning: The run's reduced health ceiling made every avoidable hit more costly. The final combat demonstrates the clearest sequencing issue: defense was delayed despite multiple attackers and low HP. Exact incoming damage is unavailable, so this does not prove that an earlier Defend would have won, but it supports a general priority of preserving HP rather than maximizing damage each turn.

title: Recover after severe max-HP loss before pursuing more upgrades
situation: After accepting a large maximum-HP penalty or reaching a campfire at roughly half health or less, especially with multiple combats still ahead.
lesson: Treat healing as the default campfire action until a meaningful HP buffer is restored. Avoid several consecutive upgrades while remaining critically low unless the upgrade is immediately necessary for survival.
evidence_points: After accepting five Apparitions on Act 2 Floor 22, maximum HP fell to 40; later campfires at Floors 27, 30, and 32 were used to smith while HP was only 24/40 to 26/40.
The Act 2 Floor 33 combat ended with only 2/40 HP, and Act 3 was ultimately entered with just 40 maximum HP.
reasoning: The upgrades strengthened the deck, but the repeated low-HP state left too little margin for ordinary fights and the Act 2 boss route. Healing earlier would have preserved flexibility and made the final boss attempt more resilient.

title: Reassess the target based on the active boss's intent
situation: In multi-enemy fights such as Donu and Deca, when one enemy is attacking and the other is defending, particularly when HP is low.
lesson: Prefer damage or debuffs against the active attacker unless another target can be killed immediately or a stronger defensive setup justifies ignoring it. Do not continue attacking the same enemy merely because it was the previous focus.
evidence_points: On Turn 6, Donu was at 110 HP with Intent ATTACK while Deca was at 163 HP with Intent DEFEND; Bash+ and Carnage+ were available against either target.
Bash+ was directed into Deca, and Immolate+ followed, leaving Donu alive at 77 HP as the attacking threat on the next turn.
reasoning: The exact incoming damage is unavailable, so the counterfactual is uncertain, but the decision left the currently attacking boss alive while single-target damage was spent on the defending boss. Target selection should be driven by current intent and lethal opportunities.

title: Keep the deck near 25 cards and stop adding marginal cards
situation: Once the deck approaches roughly 25 cards, and especially when it is already 30 or more, evaluate every reward and shop purchase against consistency rather than continuing to accumulate cards.
lesson: Aim for a compact deck of about 25 cards when possible. Skip mediocre rewards, prioritize removals, and only add cards that directly improve the current game plan or solve a specific upcoming fight. Sequence shop purchases so removal is not crowded out by lower-priority additions.
evidence_points: The final deck contained 38 cards and still had four Strikes.
At the Act 2 shop, card removal was available for 100 gold, but Orrery was purchased for 152 gold; five more card rewards were then selected on that floor.
Iron Wave+ and Whirlwind+ were both added immediately before entering the Act 3 boss portal.
reasoning: Although several additions were powerful, a 38-card deck diluted access to the Apparitions, scaling, and defensive tools that made the build work. A roughly 25-card target would have improved draw consistency and made removal more valuable than marginal late-run additions.
